raw_findings.body: Background-generated content (notification emails, digests, system posts) shows 'translation missing: ...' instead of falling back to the site default locale or English, defeating the feature this PR introduces for all non-request code paths
raw_findings.failure_mode: Fallback lookup finds no data for unloaded fallback locales and returns the missing-translation placeholder in all non-controller execution contexts
raw_findings.impact: Background-generated content (notification emails, digests, system posts) shows 'translation missing: ...' instead of falling back to the site default locale or English, defeating the feature this PR introduces for all non-request code paths
raw_findings.root_cause: Fallback locale eager-loading was wired only into ApplicationController#set_locale rather than into I18n.translate, while the lazy-loading backend cannot self-load fallback locales
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Move fallback loading into the translation path itself, e.g. have the accelerator's `translate` (or `load_locale`) call `I18n.fallbacks[locale].each { |l| ensure_loaded!(l) }` instead of relying on a controller before_filter
raw_findings.title: Fallback locales are only ensured loaded in the HTTP request cycle, so server-side fallbacks silently fail in jobs/mailers
raw_findings.trigger: A Sidekiq job or mailer (e.g. app/jobs/base.rb sets `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale`, PostAlerter uses `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)`) translates a key that is missing in the active non-English locale; the fallback locales (site default / :en) were never loaded because `ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from ApplicationController#set_locale, and the patched `Base#load_translations` no-ops on the Simple backend's lazy `init_translations`, so unloaded fallback locales just return nil

raw_findings.body: The second site is served the first site's fallback translation (e.g. German text on a French-default site), or stale fallback text persists after the default locale is changed, because the cache key omits the default_locale component of the newly locale-dependent result
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cross-site or stale cache hits return translations resolved through the wrong fallback chain
raw_findings.impact: The second site is served the first site's fallback translation (e.g. German text on a French-default site), or stale fallback text persists after the default locale is changed, because the cache key omits the default_locale component of the newly locale-dependent result
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch makes translation results depend on the mutable, per-site SiteSetting.default_locale while the pre-existing cache key only incorporates key, locale, and backend identity
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Include the resolved fallback chain (or SiteSetting.default_locale) in the accelerator cache key, or clear/namespace the cache per site and on default_locale changes
raw_findings.title: Fallback chain depends on SiteSetting.default_locale but the LRU translation cache key does not, causing wrong cached translations across multisite sites or after a default-locale change
raw_findings.trigger: A multisite process serves two sites with different `SiteSetting.default_locale` (or an admin changes default_locale at runtime); a key missing in the user locale is translated on one site, cached in the accelerator's LRU cache under `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`, then the same key/locale is requested in the other site's context

raw_findings.body: The core new behavior — missing keys resolving via user locale → site default locale → :en — is unverified, so regressions in fallback resolution or lazy loading would ship undetected
raw_findings.failure_mode: Future changes to the fallback list, initializer ordering, or the accelerator's loading logic can silently break server-side fallbacks
raw_findings.impact: The core new behavior — missing keys resolving via user locale → site default locale → :en — is unverified, so regressions in fallback resolution or lazy loading would ship undetected
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch introduces new runtime translation-resolution logic without any accompanying automated test coverage
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a spec that sets SiteSetting.default_locale to a non-English locale, requests a key present only in the default locale and only in :en, and asserts I18n.t resolves via the expected chain after ensure_loaded!
raw_findings.title: No tests added for the new server-side fallback mechanism (FallbackLocaleList / ensure_loaded!)
raw_findings.trigger: Running the existing test suite: spec/integrity/i18n_spec.rb only validates YAML structure, and no spec covers translate_accelerator or the new fallback ordering, so a regression in fallback resolution (e.g. wrong chain order, unloaded fallback locale, or the Fallbacks module not being included) passes CI

finding.trigger: A Sidekiq job or mailer (e.g. app/jobs/base.rb sets `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale`, PostAlerter uses `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)`) translates a key that is missing in the active non-English locale; the fallback locales (site default / :en) were never loaded because `ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from ApplicationController#set_locale, and the patched `Base#load_translations` no-ops on the Simple backend's lazy `init_translations`, so unloaded fallback locales just return nil
finding.verifier_reason: The patch adds `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` only in ApplicationController#set_locale (line 159), which is a before_filter for HTTP requests. The repository context confirms background jobs (app/jobs/base.rb:151) and mailers (app/services/post_alerter.rb:138 via I18n.with_locale) set I18n.locale without calling ensure_loaded!. The translate_accelerator.rb shows load_locale is called for config.locale but not for fallback locales. This means fallback locales won't be loaded in non-HTTP contexts, causing fallback resolution to fail.
